questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Personal connection to the destination (heritage / friends there/ etc.)

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: fun city, good university, chill vibe compared to at KU

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: The university was helpful with a lot of info via email. However Germany is a bit behind on digitilization, so for example most contracts are still signed by hand etc so there's a lot of travelling back and forth to different offices to get the right papers signed/stamped etc, which can be slightly confusing in the beginning. What was also a bit annoying was that some important info on e.g. how to sign up for exams came via letter only, and if you didn't receive this letter (due to DHL's bad delivery service or delays with anmeldung) you had to get the sign up code at a specific office at a specific time.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: Uni helped with Anmeldung, which is currently a three month wait at the official office in Berlin due to delays after Covid, so that was very helpful. Other than that a lot of good info via email. But finding apartment and other logistic stuff is up to one self.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: I think the uni are doing as well as they can keeping people up to speed and helping with different stuff, but bureaucracy in Germany is just on another level, which is a bit annoying. However, they should drop the "via letter only" information, as delivery service in Germany is rotten and it is very confusing how to get access to info if you haven't received the specific letters. Keep this in mind if you go on exchange to Germany, know which letters you are supposed to receive at what time

questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: Lol, housing in Berlin.. good luck! I was very lucky finding a cute WG in Prenzlauerberg via facebook, but a lot of people pay 1000 euro to live in some tiny room outside the ring without anmeldung and never see a glimse of their deposit. Start looking early to find something affordable with anmeldung.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Webpage looks like something from the 2000's, mostly in German. Other than that, OK.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You can attend any class you like for the first 2 weeks, then you register online for the ones you want to take.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: the exchange student's office I guess?

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got them all but they overlapped. Seminars are very difficult to get and you need to sign up way earlier, so keep that in mind and apply for several to have a shot

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: It's literally ONLY exchange students that take 30 ECTS during a semester. I didn't meet a single Berlin student taking more than 3 courses per semester (6 ECTS per course) as the exam period is 2 days after last lecture and all exams are happening within 2 weeks. So imagine taking 5 courses lol. Take a seminar to get somewhat of a break, those are usually due 1 month after exams

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I like econometrics and data stuff, so I was looking for more IT/blockchain/cyber security related courses, which didn't exist. But the Advanced marketing modeling was a really nice applied econometrics course in R (which is treated more like a seminar as it's term papers in stead of a closed book exam.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: Depends what you take. If the course says "Advanced", it's not as advanced as in Cph. But for only 6 ECTS it's a lot of work still

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: At CPH you calculate stuff in basically any course you take, that's not the case in all courses at Humboldt. If you take e.g. Public econ, competition policy, network based energy systems, you'll calculate micro stuff all day long. But e.g. Advanced International Trade introduces ~50 models which you don't need to calculate but interpret

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: European Economic History since 1914 until today ! Really interesting, really good professor as well. Same professor in Advanced international trade, which was also a good course. Advanced marketing modeling was also a favourite course, a little demanding but really nice in terms of applied econometrics in R

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Gas and electricity prices are insane in Germany right now, and its only summer... we went from paying 20 each in an apartment of 4 people, to paying 54 each. Internet became more expensive all of a sudden. TV bill in the mail. In general, companies really rip off ex-paths living in Berlin, you always get a worse deal if your'e not German or speaking good German.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Groceries is just as expensive in DK, that was a surprise given the wage level here. Depends where in the city you are, Mitte is 2x as pricey as Neukölln. Go to Neukölln <3

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: RAVES! This is one of the sole reasons I came here. There's a lot of good clubs and parties (and a lot of bad ones) were music is bouncing and people are super friendly. Very queer friendly city which is just super nice. People are more relaxed than in Copenhagen, you don't encounter the newest Asics or NB sneaks for 2000 dkk on people very often. Just more laid back in general. If your'e into art there are several interesting exhibitions as well and also good cinema

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Berghain

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: easy peasy lemon squeezy

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: yes. It is 100 x easier to interact with local students at HU compared with KU. Literally any foreign student at KU I've ever met has complained about how hard it is making Danish friends. That's not the case in Berlin, I met 3 German guys my first day in class whom I hung out with every day at school. Also my partey friends in another class :* just be open and chill, people are way more chill here than in Cph so you don't need to say which bank your'e dad works for and that you got a 12 in Macro III

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: The exam period. Taking 5 in one shot is literally impossible. I had several exams in the days after each other. Absolutely horrible, no time to study for them properly. Usually german students take 1-2 exams in the first period, and 1-2 in the second period. As an exchange student, you try to take all 5 in the first, which is horrible. I don't even think the uni expects anyone to do that

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Everything. The multicultural and queer vibe in the city

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Be aware of the process for settling in; find apartment with anmeldung, know which papers you will receive and when you should receive them
2. Take a seminar - to have 5 sit in exams is horrible. If possible, take less than 30 ects
3. Go out partying! It's not only about 'partying', but you'll meet some of the best people of berlin doing this. Its ok to go out alone in this city, youll meet so many friends this way. Otherwise hop on Bumble and see if you find compatibles who wanna go out. Check Resident Advisor if you don't know any places. Try both clubs and independent parties (raves), I prefer the latter

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have fun, go to events, meet people, don't take things too seriously, you'll be fine. Just have a plan with the exams lol

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people. Really some of the best friends ive ever met, after only a few months

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The exams

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: Have fun, go to events, meet people, don't take things too seriously, you'll be fine. Just have a plan with the exams lol
